A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GM-MoE, with matching architecture, benchmarks, and original experiments. All pages, including appendices and references, were readable; rendered figures, tables, and equations support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original enhancement results on five datasets, component ablations in Table 3, and qualitative enhancement and object-detection examples.

after.justification: v4 retains those original results and adds SID evaluation, LPIPS comparisons, expert heatmaps, and architecture ablations in the supplement.

M1.justification: Figure 3 revises an Expert3 convolution before SG from 1x1 to 3x3. Section 3.1 also changes Expert1's interpolation description from bilinear to nonlinear. Pooling and deconvolution were already depicted in v3, so these are not wholly new components. The overall three-expert architecture, gating, and loss remain.

E1.justification: Appendix A.3 adds evaluation on the SID dataset; v3's SID entries instead name a comparison method. The five original enhancement datasets and qualitative object-detection scenario remain. SID's precise training and testing conditions are unspecified.

E2.justification: v4 adds SCI, NeRCo, and DiffLLE to quantitative LOL-v1 comparisons, alongside newly reported LightenDiffusion scores there. Huawei Figure 9 adds PairLIE, SCI, QuadPrior, and NeRCo. The 3DLUT, Sparse, RUAS, and DRBN comparisons moved from v3 appendix Table 4 into the main tables are retained comparisons.

E3.justification: New evaluations introduce LPIPS, one-expert-at-a-time visualization, and fixed-weight, serial, and concatenation controls. Existing dataset splits, 256x256 inputs, Adam optimization, batch size four, and two million training iterations remain unchanged as reported. No detailed SID protocol is supplied.

E4.justification: Beyond retaining the incremental component ablations, v4 adds expert activation heatmaps and tests fixed gating, serial experts, and channel concatenation with 1x1 fusion. Appendix A.8 and Table 6 substantially extend scrutiny of expert coordination and whether performance depends on fusion design rather than parameter count alone.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. The new results retain the earlier single-value reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and Table 3 scores are retained apart from rounding. New outcomes include SID at 24.80 PSNR/0.69 SSIM, GM-MoE LPIPS of 0.098/0.100/0.041 across the three LOL datasets, additional comparator outputs, and architecture results. Table 6 reports serial experts at 21.34 PSNR/0.83 SSIM versus 23.65/0.80 for the full model, revealing a metric tradeoff. These are added findings, not version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: The mathematical operations underlying gating, expert fusion, interpolation, and PSNR loss remain. Equations 5–6 align SFEB symbols with Aavg, Amax, and Fw; the same fusion operations already appear in v3 and Figure 4. No new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the first-MoE-for-LLIE claim, dynamic three-expert contribution, strong generalization claim, and claimed PSNR superiority on five benchmarks and SSIM superiority on four. Changing '25' comparisons to 'over 20' does not materially alter these claims. The SSIM exceptions visible in Table 1 persist.

C2.justification: Appendix A.6 adds a spatial-complementarity interpretation of expert heatmaps. A.7 newly argues that 27.2 GFLOPs makes real-time deployment practical, whereas v3 discusses real-time enhancement as future work. The original limitations concerning expert complexity, downstream tasks, and alternative losses remain essentially unchanged in A.9.

D1.justification: v3's promise to release code after acceptance becomes a concrete repository address and availability statement in v4's abstract. v4 removes the three-day training-time disclosure while retaining hardware and main hyperparameters. It adds a 27.2 GFLOPs figure without specifying its input resolution or timing protocol; repository accessibility was not externally checked.

R1.justification: v4 adds cited works for SCI, NeRCo, and DiffLLE. The Wang et al. 2023 reference used for LLFormer in v3 disappears, while the retained Table 1 row now has an unresolved citation. Most related-work positioning remains; duplicate SID and LightenDiffusion bibliography entries do not represent new prior works.

P1.justification: There are targeted rewrites of contribution bullets, Section 2.2, Expert1 and gating explanations, and the conclusion. Author information changes, and the supplement gains named subsections and acknowledgments. The main section sequence and most existing prose remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from one column to two columns, with redrawn architecture and SFEB diagrams and extensive resizing and relocation. Figure 2 drops its LOLv2-Real panel while table results remain. The old appendix Table 4 is merged into Tables 1–2; new Tables 4–6 and Figure 12 are added, and Huawei Figure 9 expands.

improvement.justification: LPIPS comparisons and the approximately parameter-matched gating/fusion controls improve evidence for perceptual quality and the central design beyond v3's component ablations. Concrete code-access information also helps reproducibility. The net gain is limited: SID lacks a defined protocol, real-time feasibility is asserted without timings, and LLFormer's citation becomes broken. Existing broad superiority claims also remain insufficiently qualified.
